state:
Goal `core-metrics-and-4-more`, stage 2, per-member feature proofs. `Core\Metrics` and `Core\Mime`
are done and their group checks pass. All three classes this goal still owes now have their class
cards (`Core\Net`, `Core\Net\Datagram`, `Core\Net\Datagram\Message`), so no member owes help any more.
`Core\Net::connect` and `Core\Net::listen` carry every proof, perf recorded. `Core\Net::bindDatagram`,
`connectLocal` and `listenLocal` still owe examples, hostile, perf and a Rust `covers:` marker. The
`Datagram` and `Message` members owe every proof except help. A proof directory may now carry an
`nvs.toml` that the runner passes as `--config` (`docs/examples/README.md` § *A grant the examples
need*). This is how a `Core\Net` example gets a loopback grant. Nothing is blocked.

next.note: one file set: `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/net.rs`, and the `core/Net/` directories under `docs/examples/`, `tests/hostile/` and `benches/members/`, each with its `nvs.toml` grant (copy `docs/examples/core/Net/connect/nvs.toml`).

items.text: **`Core\Net::bindDatagram`** — about, 3 examples, hostile, bench and a `covers:` marker (`rule:testing/feature-proofs`). Put the marker on the UDP test at `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/net.rs:2082`. The member is at `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/net.rs:1720`. Its grant is `listen = ["127.0.0.1:0"]`, and `send` also needs `connect`/`internal = ["127.0.0.1"]`. After the marker, record perf again for `connect` and `listen` with `bun nv proofs --record-perf --id`, because the record is keyed on the bytes of `net.rs`.

**`Core\Net::connectLocal` and `Core\Net::listenLocal`** — the same proofs. The members are at `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/net.rs:1422` and `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/net.rs:1452`, and the marker goes on `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/net.rs:2210`. Windows has no `AF_UNIX` transport, so a granted call prints something different on Windows and Linux. Keep the examples and the attack to the not-granted path and the argument checks, which run before the transport check and print the same on both. A bench cannot run a real local socket on Windows. Decide between a bench of the refusal path and a `skip` entry in `data/proofs/policy.json`, and say why in the commit.

**`Core\Net\Datagram`'s four members and `Core\Net\Datagram\Message`'s three** — every proof except help. The classes are at `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/net.rs:756` and `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/net.rs:928`. Directories are `core/Net-Datagram/<member>` and `core/Net-Datagram-Message/<member>`. Each needs its own `nvs.toml`, and a bench directory needs one per class directory.

backlog: `Core\Net::connect` costs about 15.5 ms per call over loopback on Windows (`docs/perf/members.ndjson`), about one Windows timer tick. `listen` costs 56 µs. The cause is not checked. A blocking connect path that polls with a sleep would give this figure. Owner: `nvs_host::net`'s `connect_timeout`.
Map-typed locals (`array<string, uint>`) do not parse. An example that needs a map uses a helper class instead. Not checked against the spec.
